muscles.name: PectoralisMinor
muscles.origin: Margins of the 3rd to 5th ribs, adjacent to their costochondral junctions.
muscles.insertion: Medial border and superior surface of the coracoid process of the scapula.
muscles.action: Stabilizes the scapula by drawing it downward and anteriorly against the thoracic wall: depression, protraction and downward rotation. Assists inspiration when the scapula is fixed.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial pectoral nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: SerratusAnterior
muscles.origin: Superolateral surfaces of the 1st to 8th ribs, sometimes reaching the 9th, on the lateral thoracic wall.
muscles.insertion: Anterior surface of the medial border of the scapula, from the superior to the inferior angle.
muscles.action: Draws the scapula forward around the thorax - protraction - and its inferior part rotates the scapula upward to allow elevation of the arm above the head. Holds the medial border against the thoracic wall; assists respiration when the shoulder girdle is fixed.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Long thoracic nerve (C5-C7)

muscles.name: Subclavius
muscles.origin: Junction of the 1st rib and its costal cartilage, anterior to the costoclavicular ligament.
muscles.insertion: Subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle.
muscles.action: Depresses the clavicle and anchors it at the sternoclavicular joint; assists elevation of the 1st rib.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to subclavius, also called the subclavian nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: LevatorScapulae
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of C1-C4, from their posterior tubercles.
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the scapula, from the superior angle to the root of the scapular spine.
muscles.action: Scapular elevation, retraction and downward rotation of the glenoid cavity; stabilizes the scapula during movement. Acting on the neck: unilateral lateral flexion toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5), with direct branches from the anterior rami of C3-C4

muscles.name: Rhomboids(major&minor)
muscles.origin: Minor: lower ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7-T1 with their supraspinous ligaments. Major: spinous processes of T2-T5.
muscles.insertion: Minor: medial border of the scapula at the level of the scapular spine. Major: medial border between the scapular spine and the inferior angle.
muscles.action: Scapular retraction, drawing it medially and superiorly, with downward rotation of the glenoid cavity. Hold the medial border against the thoracic wall.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Dorsal scapular nerve (C4-C5)

muscles.name: Trapezius(upper)
muscles.origin: External occipital protuberance, medial third of the superior nuchal line, and the ligamentum nuchae, which itself attaches to the spinous processes of C1-C6.
muscles.insertion: Posterior border of the lateral third of the clavicle.
muscles.action: Scapular elevation, retraction (adduction), and upward rotation. Bilateral: extension of the head and neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation of the face away.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with proprioceptive fibers from C3-C4

muscles.name: Trapezius(middle)
muscles.origin: Spinous processes and supraspinous ligaments of C6-T3.
muscles.insertion: Medial margin of the acromion and the superior crest of the scapular spine.
muscles.action: Scapular retraction, drawing it medially, with assistance in upward rotation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with sensory and proprioceptive fibers from the ventral rami of C3-C4

muscles.name: Trapezius(lower)
muscles.origin: Spinous processes and supraspinous ligaments of T4-T12.
muscles.insertion: Aponeurosis at the medial end of the scapular spine, onto its tubercle.
muscles.action: Scapular depression, retraction (adduction), and upward rotation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with proprioceptive fibers from C3-C4

muscles.name: PectoralisMajor(clavicularhead)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder flexion to approximately 90 degrees, horizontal adduction, and internal rotation. Assists adduction when the arm is abducted less than 90 degrees.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral pectoral nerve (C5-C7)

muscles.name: PectoralisMajor(sternalhead)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the sternum and the costal cartilages of the 1st-6th ribs; the lowest fibers arise from the aponeurosis of the external oblique.
muscles.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder adduction, horizontal adduction, and internal rotation. Extends the flexed arm back toward the anatomical position.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial and lateral pectoral nerves (C7-T1)

muscles.name: Deltoid(anteriorhead)
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the lateral third of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder flexion and internal rotation; horizontal adduction. Works with pectoralis major to flex the arm during walking.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: Deltoid(middlehead)
muscles.origin: Superolateral surface of the acromion of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder abduction, raising the arm from roughly 15 to 100 degrees. It cannot initiate abduction because it contracts parallel to the humeral axis; supraspinatus performs the first 15 degrees.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: Deltoid(posteriorhead)
muscles.origin: Inferior border of the spine of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity on the lateral surface of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder extension and external rotation; horizontal abduction. Works with latissimus dorsi to extend the arm during walking.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: LatissimusDorsi
muscles.origin: Lateral sides of the spinous processes of T7-T12, the thoracolumbar fascia, the posterior iliac crest, and the proximal third of the 9th-12th ribs.
muscles.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder adduction, extension and internal rotation; horizontal abduction. Raises the trunk toward the arm when the humerus is fixed, as in climbing, and is active in forced expiration.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Thoracodorsal nerve (C6-C8)

muscles.name: TeresMajor
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the inferior angle and lower third of the lateral border of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular (bicipital) groove of the humerus.
muscles.action: Shoulder extension, adduction and internal rotation; assists in stabilizing the humeral head.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lower subscapular nerve (C5-C7)

muscles.name: Coracobrachialis
muscles.origin: Apex of the coracoid process of the scapula, shared with the short head of biceps brachii.
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humeral shaft.
muscles.action: Shoulder flexion and weak adduction.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C7)

muscles.name: Supraspinatus (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Supraspinous fossa of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.
muscles.action: Initiates shoulder abduction through the first 15 degrees, before the deltoid can act; stabilizes the humeral head in the glenoid cavity.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Suprascapular nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: Infraspinatus (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Infraspinous fossa of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus, below the supraspinatus attachment.
muscles.action: External rotation of the humerus - the most powerful external rotator; stabilizes the humeral head in the glenoid cavity.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Suprascapular nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: TeresMinor (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Upper part of the posterior surface of the lateral border of the scapula, below the infraglenoid tubercle.
muscles.insertion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus, below the infraspinatus tendon.
muscles.action: External rotation of the humerus; stabilizes the glenohumeral joint as part of the rotator cuff.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Axillary nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: Subscapularis (*rotator cuff muscle group)
muscles.origin: Medial two-thirds of the subscapular fossa on the anterior surface of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Lesser tubercle of the humerus.
muscles.action: Internal rotation of the humerus; prevents anterior displacement of the humeral head during abduction. Assists adduction and extension from certain positions.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5-C7)

muscles.name: BicepsBrachii
muscles.origin: Long head: supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and the superior glenoid labrum. Short head: apex of the coracoid process of the scapula.
muscles.insertion: Radial tuberosity, with the bicipital aponeurosis spreading medially into the deep fascia of the forearm.
muscles.action: Powerful supination of the forearm, strongest with the elbow flexed; elbow flexion, in which it is a weaker contributor than brachialis. Assists shoulder flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5-C6)

muscles.name: Brachialis
muscles.origin: Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus.
muscles.insertion: Ulnar tuberosity and the coronoid process of the ulna.
muscles.action: Pure elbow flexion, with no pronation or supination component. The primary elbow flexor, and the only one unaffected by forearm position.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve medially, with a radial nerve contribution laterally (C5-C7)

muscles.name: Brachioradialis
muscles.origin: Proximal two-thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
muscles.insertion: Base of the styloid process on the lateral surface of the distal radius.
muscles.action: Elbow flexion, most effective with the forearm in mid-pronation. Returns the forearm toward neutral from either extreme: pronates from a supinated position, supinates from a pronated one.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Radial nerve (C5-C7, predominantly C5-C6)

muscles.name: PronatorTeres
muscles.origin: Humeral head: medial supracondylar ridge just above the medial epicondyle. Ulnar head: coronoid process of the ulna.
muscles.insertion: Pronator tuberosity on the lateral surface of the midshaft of the radius.
muscles.action: Forearm pronation; small contribution to elbow flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Median nerve (C6-C7)

muscles.name: PronatorQuadratus
muscles.origin: Distal quarter of the anteromedial surface of the ulna.
muscles.insertion: Distal quarter of the anterolateral surface of the radius.
muscles.action: Forearm pronation; the prime mover, with pronator teres recruited against resistance. Holds the radius and ulna together at the distal radioulnar joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the median nerve (C8-T1)
muscles.review_flag: nerve root levels rest on a single source

muscles.name: Supinator
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus, the radial collateral and annular ligaments, and the supinator crest of the ulna.
muscles.insertion: Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of the proximal third of the radius.
muscles.action: Forearm supination; acts alone in unresisted supination, with biceps brachii recruited against resistance.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C6-C7)

muscles.name: Anconeus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, at the common extensor origin.
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the olecranon and the upper posterior surface of the ulna.
muscles.action: Assists elbow extension and stabilizes the joint; draws the joint capsule clear of the advancing olecranon. Abducts the ulna during pronation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Radial nerve (C7-C8), by a branch given off before the posterior interosseous nerve

muscles.name: TricepsBrachii
muscles.origin: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. Lateral head: posterior surface of the humerus above the radial groove. Medial head: posterior surface of the humerus below the radial groove.
muscles.insertion: Olecranon of the ulna, by a common tendon.
muscles.action: All heads: elbow extension. Long head additionally: shoulder extension and adduction, and it holds the humeral head in the glenoid cavity.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Radial nerve (C6-C8)

muscles.name: FlexorPollicisLongus
muscles.origin: Middle third of the anterior surface of the radius and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Palmar surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
muscles.action: Flexion of the interphalangeal joint of the thumb, and of the metacarpophalangeal joint; assists wrist flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the median nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: FlexorDigitorumProfundus
muscles.origin: Proximal three-quarters of the anterior and medial surfaces of the ulna and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Palmar surfaces of the bases of the distal phalanges of the four fingers.
muscles.action: The only muscle able to flex the distal interphalangeal joints; also flexes the proximal interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal and wrist joints.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Radial half, to the index and middle fingers: anterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the median nerve (C8-T1). Ulnar half, to the ring and little fingers: ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: FlexorDigitorumSuperficialis
muscles.origin: Humero-ulnar head: medial epicondyle of the humerus and the coronoid process of the ulna. Radial head: anterior oblique line of the radius.
muscles.insertion: Each tendon splits around the flexor digitorum profundus tendon and its two slips attach to the sides of the shaft (body) of the middle phalanx of the four fingers.
muscles.action: Flexion of the fingers at the proximal interphalangeal joints, and at the metacarpophalangeal joints; assists wrist flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Median nerve (C7-T1)

muscles.name: FlexorCarpiUlnaris
muscles.origin: Humeral head: medial epicondyle of the humerus. Ulnar head: olecranon and proximal two-thirds of the posterior border of the ulna.
muscles.insertion: Pisiform, and by the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments to the hook of the hamate and the base of the 5th metacarpal.
muscles.action: Wrist flexion and ulnar deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: FlexorCarpiRadialis
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus, by the common flexor tendon.
muscles.insertion: Palmar surfaces of the bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals.
muscles.action: Wrist flexion and radial deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Median nerve (C6-C7)

muscles.name: PalmarisLongus
muscles.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus, by the common flexor tendon.
muscles.insertion: Flexor retinaculum and the palmar aponeurosis.
muscles.action: Wrist flexion; tenses the palmar aponeurosis.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Median nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: ExtensorCarpiRadialisLongus
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 2nd metacarpal.
muscles.action: Wrist extension and radial deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Radial nerve (C6-C7)

muscles.name: ExtensorCarpiRadialisBrevis
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus, by the common extensor tendon.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 3rd metacarpal.
muscles.action: Wrist extension and radial deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Radial nerve (C6-C8); commonly described as reaching it through the deep branch

muscles.name: ExtensorDigitorum
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus, by the common extensor tendon.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hoods of the four fingers, reaching the bases of the middle and distal phalanges.
muscles.action: Extension of the fingers at the metacarpophalangeal joints, and at the interphalangeal joints together with the interossei and lumbricals; assists wrist extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: ExtensorCarpiUlnaris
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus and the posterior border of the ulna.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 5th metacarpal.
muscles.action: Wrist extension and ulnar deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: ExtensorDigitiMinimi
muscles.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus, by the common extensor tendon.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hood of the little finger.
muscles.action: Extension of the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints; assists wrist extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: AbductorPollicisLongus
muscles.origin: Posterior surfaces of the middle third of the ulna and radius and the intervening interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Base of the 1st metacarpal, with a slip to the trapezium.
muscles.action: Abduction of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint, with extension; assists wrist radial deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: ExtensorPollicisLongus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the middle third of the ulna and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb.
muscles.action: Extension of the thumb at the interphalangeal, metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints; assists wrist extension and radial deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: ExtensorPollicisBrevis
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the distal third of the radius and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
muscles.action: Extension of the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal and carpometacarpal joints; assists wrist extension and radial deviation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: ExtensorIndicis
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the distal third of the ulna and the adjacent interosseous membrane, below the origin of extensor pollicis longus.
muscles.insertion: Extensor hood of the index finger.
muscles.action: Extension of the index finger independently of the other fingers; assists wrist extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior interosseous nerve, the deep branch of the radial nerve (C7-C8)

muscles.name: AbductorPollicisBrevis
muscles.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium.
muscles.insertion: Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
muscles.action: Abduction of the thumb at the carpometacarpal and metacarpophalangeal joints; contributes to opposition.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: OpponensPollicis
muscles.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium.
muscles.insertion: Whole length of the lateral border of the 1st metacarpal.
muscles.action: Opposition of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint, by flexing and medially rotating the metacarpal so the thumb pad faces the fingers.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: FlexorPollicisBrevis
muscles.origin: Superficial head: flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium. Deep head: trapezoid and capitate, with a slip from the 2nd metacarpal.
muscles.insertion: Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, over a sesamoid bone.
muscles.action: Flexion of the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint; assists flexion and opposition at the carpometacarpal joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superficial head: recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8-T1). Deep head: deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: AbductorDigitiMinimi
muscles.origin: Pisiform and the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris.
muscles.insertion: Ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger.
muscles.action: Abduction of the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: FlexorDigitiMinimi
muscles.origin: Hook of the hamate and the adjacent flexor retinaculum.
muscles.insertion: Ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger.
muscles.action: Flexion of the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: OpponensDigitiMinimi
muscles.origin: Hook of the hamate and the adjacent flexor retinaculum.
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the 5th metacarpal.
muscles.action: Draws the 5th metacarpal forward and rotates it toward the thumb - flexion and supination of the metacarpal - deepening the hollow of the palm.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: AdductorPollicis
muscles.origin: Oblique head: capitate and the bases of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals. Transverse head: palmar surface of the shaft of the 3rd metacarpal.
muscles.insertion: Ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb and the extensor hood, over a sesamoid bone.
muscles.action: Adduction of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint; assists flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: Dorsal Interossei (Hand)
muscles.origin: Each by two heads from the adjacent sides of the shafts of two metacarpals: the 1st from metacarpals 1-2, the 2nd from 2-3, the 3rd from 3-4, the 4th from 4-5.
muscles.insertion: Lateral bases of the proximal phalanges and the extensor hoods of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th fingers.
muscles.action: Abduction of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th fingers away from the axis of the hand, taken through the middle finger; assists flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joints and extension at the interphalangeal joints.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: Palmar Interossei (Hand)
muscles.origin: Palmar surfaces of the 2nd (ulnar side), 4th and 5th (radial side) metacarpals.
muscles.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and the extensor hoods of the same fingers.
muscles.action: Adduction of the fingers toward the axis of the hand, taken through the middle finger; assists flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joints and extension at the interphalangeal joints.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: Lumbricals (Hand)
muscles.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus in the palm: the 1st and 2nd from the radial side of the tendons to the index and middle fingers, the 3rd and 4th by two heads from adjacent tendons.
muscles.insertion: Radial side of the extensor hood of the 2nd to 5th fingers, by the lateral bands.
muscles.action: Flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joints with simultaneous extension at the interphalangeal joints, by pulling on the extensor hood.
muscles.nerve_innervation: 1st and 2nd: median nerve (C8-T1). 3rd and 4th: deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8-T1)

muscles.name: Sternocleidomastoid
muscles.origin: Sternal head: superior part of the anterior surface of the manubrium. Clavicular head: superior surface of the medial third of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the mastoid process, continuing onto the lateral half of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
muscles.action: Bilateral: flexes the lower cervical spine while extending the head at the atlanto-occipital joint; assists inspiration by raising the sternum and clavicle. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation of the face to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Accessory nerve (CN XI) for motor supply, with proprioceptive fibers from the cervical plexus (C2-C3)

muscles.name: Scalenes(Anterior,Middle,Posterior)
muscles.origin: Anterior: anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3-C6. Middle: lateral parts of the atlas and axis and the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C3-C7. Posterior: posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C5-C7.
muscles.insertion: Anterior: scalene tubercle on the superior surface of the 1st rib, in front of the groove for the subclavian artery. Middle: superior surface of the 1st rib behind that groove, in the quadrangular area between the neck of the rib and the subclavian groove. Posterior: outer surface of the 2nd rib.
muscles.action: Bilateral: cervical flexion; elevate the 1st and 2nd ribs in forced inspiration; contribute to postural stability of the neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of the cervical spinal nerves (anterior C5-C6; middle C3-C8; posterior C6-C8)

muscles.name: SpleniusCervicis
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T3-T6.
muscles.insertion: Transverse processes of the atlas and axis and the posterior tubercle of C3.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion and rotation toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the lower cervical spinal nerves

muscles.name: SpleniusCapitis
muscles.origin: Lower half of the ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7-T3, with their supraspinous ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Lateral aspect of the mastoid process and the lateral third of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the head and neck. Unilateral: lateral flexion and rotation toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the upper cervical spinal nerves (C2-C3)

muscles.name: SemispinalisCapitis
muscles.origin: Articular processes of C4-C6 and the transverse processes of C7-T7.
muscles.insertion: Medial half of the occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the head and neck. Unilateral: extension, lateral flexion, and weak rotation to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent cervical spinal nerves, including the greater occipital nerve (C2)

muscles.name: SemispinalisCervicis
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of T1-T6.
muscles.insertion: Spinous processes of C2-C5.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the neck. Unilateral: extension, lateral flexion, and weak rotation to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent cervical spinal nerves

muscles.name: RectusCapitisPosterior(MajorandMinor)
muscles.origin: Major: bifid spinous process of the axis (C2). Minor: posterior arch of the atlas (C1).
muscles.insertion: Major: occipital bone below the lateral part of the inferior nuchal line. Minor: occipital bone below the inferior nuchal line, medial to the major.
muscles.action: Major: head extension and rotation toward the contracting side, acting on the atlas as well as the head. Minor: weak head extension only.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Suboccipital nerve, the posterior ramus of C1

muscles.name: ObliquusCapitis(SuperiorandInferior)
muscles.origin: Superior: transverse process of the atlas (C1). Inferior: bifid spinous process of the axis (C2), below the origin of rectus capitis posterior major.
muscles.insertion: Superior: occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines. Inferior: transverse process of the atlas (C1).
muscles.action: Superior: head extension and lateral flexion toward the contracting side. Inferior: rotation of the atlas, and with it the head, toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Suboccipital nerve, the posterior ramus of C1

muscles.name: Rotatores
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of the vertebrae, from C2 to S1, though the muscles are inconstant outside the thoracic region.
muscles.insertion: Lamina and base of the spinous process of the vertebra one or two levels above.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension and segmental stabilization of the vertebral column. Unilateral: rotation to the opposite side. Their high muscle-spindle density suggests a substantial proprioceptive role.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent spinal nerves

muscles.name: Multifidus
muscles.origin: Cervical: superior articular processes of C4-C7. Thoracic: transverse processes. Lumbar: mammillary processes, posterior surface of the sacrum, posterior superior iliac spine and the posterior sacroiliac ligament.
muscles.insertion: Lateral aspect and tips of the spinous processes of vertebrae two to four levels above the origin.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension and segmental stabilization of the vertebral column. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side and rotation to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent spinal nerves

muscles.name: QuadratusLumborum
muscles.origin: Inner lip of the iliac crest and the iliolumbar ligament.
muscles.insertion: Internal surface of the 12th rib and the transverse processes of L1-L4.
muscles.action: Bilateral: lumbar extension; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt. Unilateral: lumbar lateral flexion and elevation of the pelvis on the same side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Subcostal nerve (T12), with the iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1)

muscles.name: ErectorSpinae:Spinalis(Thoracis,Cervicis)
muscles.origin: Thoracis: spinous processes of T11-L2. Cervicis: lower ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7-T1.
muscles.insertion: Thoracis: spinous processes of T2-T8. Cervicis: spinous processes of C2-C4.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the vertebral column; maintains posture. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent spinal nerves

muscles.name: ErectorSpinae:Longissimus(Thoracis,Cervicis,Capitis)
muscles.origin: Thoracis: posteromedial sacrum, posterior iliac crest, thoracolumbar aponeurosis and the transverse processes of L1-L5. Cervicis: transverse processes of T1-T5. Capitis: transverse processes of T1-T5 and the articular processes of C5-C7.
muscles.insertion: Thoracis: transverse processes of T1-T12 and the 4th-12th ribs. Cervicis: transverse processes of C2-C6. Capitis: posterior margin of the mastoid process.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the head and vertebral column; maintains posture; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt. Unilateral: lateral flexion and rotation toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent spinal nerves

muscles.name: ErectorSpinae:Iliocostalis(Lumborum,Thoracis,Cervicis)
muscles.origin: Lumborum: posteromedial iliac crest, lateral crest of the sacrum and the thoracolumbar aponeurosis. Thoracis: angles of the 7th-12th ribs. Cervicis: angles of the 3rd-6th ribs.
muscles.insertion: Lumborum: angles of the 5th-12th ribs and the transverse processes of L1-L4. Thoracis: angles of the 1st-6th ribs and the transverse process of C7. Cervicis: transverse processes of C4-C6.
muscles.action: Bilateral: extension of the vertebral column; maintains posture; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt. Unilateral: lateral flexion of the neck and trunk toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of the adjacent spinal nerves

muscles.name: RectusAbdominis
muscles.origin: Pubic crest, pubic tubercle and the pubic symphysis.
muscles.insertion: Xiphoid process and the costal cartilages of the 5th-7th ribs.
muscles.action: Bilateral: powerful flexion of the vertebral column; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt; depresses the ribs; raises intra-abdominal pressure. Unilateral: lateral flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T7-T11 (thoracoabdominal nerves) and T12 (subcostal nerve)

muscles.name: ExternalOblique
muscles.origin: External surfaces and inferior borders of the 5th-12th ribs.
muscles.insertion: Anterior half of the iliac crest, and by the abdominal aponeurosis into the linea alba, pubic crest and pubic tubercle; its lower border forms the inguinal ligament.
muscles.action: Bilateral: flexion of the vertebral column; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt; compresses the abdominal contents. Unilateral: lateral flexion toward the contracting side with rotation of the trunk to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T7-T11 (thoracoabdominal nerves) and T12 (subcostal nerve)

muscles.name: InternalOblique
muscles.origin: Thoracolumbar fascia, anterior two-thirds of the iliac crest, and the lateral half of the inguinal ligament.
muscles.insertion: Inferior borders of the 10th-12th ribs, and by the abdominal aponeurosis into the rectus sheath and linea alba, reaching the pubic crest by the conjoint tendon.
muscles.action: Bilateral: flexion of the vertebral column; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt; compresses the abdominal contents. Unilateral: lateral flexion and rotation of the trunk toward the contracting side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T7-T11, T12 (subcostal), and the iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1)

muscles.name: Transverse Abdominis
muscles.origin: Internal surfaces of the costal cartilages of the 7th-12th ribs (the lower six), thoracolumbar fascia, inner lip of the iliac crest, and the lateral third of the inguinal ligament.
muscles.insertion: Linea alba by the abdominal aponeurosis and rectus sheath, and the pubic crest by the conjoint tendon.
muscles.action: Compresses the abdominal contents and raises intra-abdominal pressure - abdominal hollowing. Contributes no significant trunk movement.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T7-T11, T12 (subcostal), and the iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves (L1)

muscles.name: SerratusPosteriorSuperior
muscles.origin: Lower ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7-T3 with their supraspinous ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Posterosuperior surfaces of the 2nd-5th ribs, lateral to their angles.
muscles.action: Elevates the 2nd-5th ribs; accessory muscle of inspiration.
muscles.nerve_innervation: 2nd-5th intercostal nerves

muscles.name: SerratusPosteriorInferior
muscles.origin: Spinous processes of T11-L2 and their supraspinous ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Inferoposterior surfaces of the 9th-12th ribs, lateral to their angles.
muscles.action: Depresses the lower ribs; accessory muscle of expiration.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of T9-T11 and the subcostal nerve (T12)

muscles.name: ExternalIntercostals
muscles.origin: Inferior borders of the 1st-11th ribs, running from the rib tubercle posteriorly to the costochondral junction anteriorly.
muscles.insertion: Superior borders of the 2nd-12th ribs, the fibers running inferomedially.
muscles.action: Elevate the ribs during inspiration, increasing the transverse diameter of the thorax; resist indrawing of the intercostal spaces in quiet breathing.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Intercostal nerves, the anterior rami of T1-T11

muscles.name: InternalIntercostals
muscles.origin: Costal groove of the 1st-11th ribs and the adjacent costal cartilages, running from the sternum anteriorly to the rib angles posteriorly.
muscles.insertion: Superior borders of the 2nd-12th ribs, the fibers running inferolaterally.
muscles.action: Depress the ribs during forced expiration; stabilize the ribs in quiet breathing.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Intercostal nerves, the anterior rami of T1-T11

muscles.name: LevatorCostarum
muscles.origin: Transverse processes of C7-T11.
muscles.insertion: External surface of the rib one level below, between the tubercle and the angle; the lower four also send a longer slip two levels down.
muscles.action: Elevate the ribs, contributing minimally to inspiration. Assist rotation and lateral flexion of the thoracic spine.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral branches of the posterior (dorsal) rami of C7-T11
muscles.review_flag: nerve root levels rest on a single source

muscles.name: Diaphragm
muscles.origin: Sternal part: two slips from the posterior surface of the xiphoid process. Costal part: internal surfaces of the lower six costal cartilages and adjacent ribs. Lumbar part: right crus from the bodies of L1-L3, left crus from L1-L2, with the medial and lateral arcuate ligaments.
muscles.insertion: Central tendon of the diaphragm.
muscles.action: The principal muscle of inspiration: contraction pulls the central tendon inferiorly and flattens the dome, increasing the vertical dimension of the thoracic cavity. Raises intra-abdominal pressure during straining.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Phrenic nerve (C3-C5), with sensory supply to the periphery from the lower intercostal nerves

muscles.name: TransverseThoracis
muscles.origin: Internal surface of the lower sternum and the xiphoid process.
muscles.insertion: Internal surfaces of the costal cartilages of the 2nd-6th ribs.
muscles.action: Draws the 2nd-6th costal cartilages toward the sternum, weakly depressing the ribs during forced expiration; supports the intercostal spaces.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Intercostal nerves (T2-T6)

muscles.name: Iliacus
muscles.origin: Upper two-thirds of the iliac fossa, with slips from the ala of the sacrum and the anterior sacroiliac ligament.
muscles.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, by the tendon shared with psoas major, and the adjacent shaft.
muscles.action: Hip flexion - a prime mover; stabilizes the pelvis during hip flexion and assists trunk flexion when the limb is fixed. Anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)

muscles.name: PsoasMajor
muscles.origin: Lateral surfaces of the bodies of T12-L5 and the intervening intervertebral discs, and the transverse processes of all five lumbar vertebrae.
muscles.insertion: Lesser trochanter of the femur, by the tendon shared with iliacus.
muscles.action: Hip flexion - a prime mover; assists adduction and external rotation. Stabilizes the lumbar spine in sitting; lumbar flexion and lateral flexion; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of L1-L3, directly from the lumbar plexus rather than through a named nerve

muscles.name: PsoasMinor
muscles.origin: Body of the last thoracic vertebra, the first lumbar vertebra, and the intervening intervertebral disc.
muscles.insertion: Iliopectineal eminence and the iliac fascia.
muscles.action: Weak flexion of the lumbar spine. Acts on the vertebral column only - it has no femoral attachment and does not move the hip.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of L1-L2

muscles.name: Pectineus
muscles.origin: Pecten pubis on the superior ramus of the pubis.
muscles.insertion: Pectineal line on the posterior femur, from the lesser trochanter to the linea aspera.
muscles.action: Hip flexion and adduction; assists external rotation; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L3), often with an additional branch from the obturator nerve

muscles.name: RectusFemoris
muscles.origin: Straight head: anterior inferior iliac spine. Reflected head: groove above the acetabulum.
muscles.insertion: Base of the patella by the quadriceps tendon, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension and hip flexion - the only quadriceps component crossing both joints; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)

muscles.name: Sartorius
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and the area just below it.
muscles.insertion: Superomedial surface of the proximal tibia, as the most anterior of the three pes anserinus tendons.
muscles.action: Hip flexion, abduction and external rotation; knee flexion and internal rotation; anterior pelvic rotation and tilt. Produces the cross-legged sitting posture it is named for.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)

muscles.name: Gracilis
muscles.origin: Anterior body and inferior ramus of the pubis.
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the proximal tibia at the pes anserinus, as the middle of its three tendons.
muscles.action: Hip adduction and flexion; knee flexion and internal rotation.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior branch (L2-L4)

muscles.name: TensorFasciaeLatae
muscles.origin: Anterior superior iliac spine and the outer lip of the anterior iliac crest.
muscles.insertion: Iliotibial tract, which continues to the lateral condyle of the tibia at Gerdy's tubercle.
muscles.action: Hip: internal rotation, abduction and flexion; stabilizes the pelvis in standing and gait. Knee: through the iliotibial tract, assists flexion and lateral (external) rotation of the leg, and steadies the knee.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.name: AdductorBrevis
muscles.origin: Body of the pubis and the anteroinferior pubic ramus.
muscles.insertion: Upper third of the linea aspera and the posterior proximal femur.
muscles.action: Hip adduction and flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior branch (L2-L4)

muscles.name: AdductorLongus
muscles.origin: Body of the pubis and the anteroinferior pubic ramus, just below the pubic crest.
muscles.insertion: Middle third of the linea aspera on the femoral shaft.
muscles.action: Hip adduction and flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, anterior branch (L2-L4)

muscles.name: AdductorMagnus
muscles.origin: Adductor (pubofemoral) part: inferior ramus of the pubis, ramus of the ischium, and the external obturator membrane. Hamstring (ischiocondylar) part: ischial tuberosity.
muscles.insertion: Adductor part: medial side of the gluteal tuberosity, the whole length of the linea aspera, and the medial supracondylar line. Hamstring part: adductor tubercle on the medial femoral condyle.
muscles.action: Adductor part: hip adduction, its superior segment also flexing the thigh. Hamstring part: hip adduction and extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Adductor part: obturator nerve, posterior branch (L2-L4). Hamstring part: tibial division of the sciatic nerve

muscles.name: Gluteus Minimus
muscles.origin: Gluteal surface of the ilium, between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines.
muscles.insertion: Anterior aspect of the greater trochanter of the femur.
muscles.action: Hip abduction and internal rotation; assists flexion. With gluteus medius, stabilizes the pelvis over the stance limb during gait.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.name: GluteusMedius
muscles.origin: Gluteal surface of the ilium, between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines.
muscles.insertion: Lateral aspect of the greater trochanter of the femur, by fibrocartilage.
muscles.action: Hip abduction; anterior fibers internally rotate the thigh, posterior fibers externally rotate it with the knee extended. Holds the pelvis level over the stance limb - its failure produces the Trendelenburg sign, in which the pelvis sinks on the UNSUPPORTED side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.name: GluteusMaximus
muscles.origin: Gluteal surface of the ilium behind the posterior gluteal line, lateroposterior surface of the sacrum and coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament, and the thoracolumbar fascia.
muscles.insertion: Superficial fibers into the iliotibial tract; the deep quarter into the gluteal tuberosity of the femur, between adductor magnus and vastus lateralis.
muscles.action: Hip extension and external rotation. An antigravity muscle recruited in rising from sitting, stair climbing and running rather than level walking; extends the trunk from a flexed position and stabilizes the pelvis in upright posture. Upper fibers abduct, lower fibers adduct.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Inferior gluteal nerve (L5-S2) - the only muscle this nerve supplies

muscles.name: Semitendinosus
muscles.origin: Inferomedial impression of the ischial tuberosity, by a tendon shared with the long head of biceps femoris.
muscles.insertion: Anteromedial surface of the proximal tibia below the medial condyle, as the most posterior of the three pes anserinus tendons.
muscles.action: Hip extension; knee flexion and internal rotation of the flexed knee; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2)

muscles.name: Semimembranosus
muscles.origin: Superolateral impression of the ischial tuberosity, separate from and deep to the conjoint tendon of semitendinosus and biceps femoris.
muscles.insertion: Posteromedial surface of the medial tibial condyle, with expansions into the oblique popliteal ligament and the popliteal fascia.
muscles.action: Hip extension; knee flexion and internal rotation of the flexed knee; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2)

muscles.name: BicepsFemoris
muscles.origin: Long head: ischial tuberosity, by the conjoint tendon shared with semitendinosus. Short head: lateral lip of the linea aspera and the proximal lateral supracondylar ridge of the femur.
muscles.insertion: Head of the fibula, with slips to the lateral tibial condyle and the fibular collateral ligament.
muscles.action: Long head: hip extension and external rotation. Both heads: knee flexion and external rotation of the flexed knee; posterior pelvic rotation and tilt.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Long head: tibial division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2). Short head: common fibular (peroneal) division of the sciatic nerve (L5-S2)

muscles.name: VastusLateralis
muscles.origin: Intertrochanteric line, greater trochanter, gluteal tuberosity, and the lateral lip of the linea aspera.
muscles.insertion: Lateral border of the patella by the quadriceps tendon, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension; its oblique distal fibers draw the patella laterally, opposed by vastus medialis.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)

muscles.name: VastusIntermedius
muscles.origin: Anterolateral surface of the upper two-thirds of the femoral shaft.
muscles.insertion: Deep surface of the quadriceps tendon at the proximal border of the patella, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)

muscles.name: VastusMedialis
muscles.origin: Intertrochanteric line, medial lip of the linea aspera, medial supracondylar line, and the tendon of adductor magnus.
muscles.insertion: Medial border of the patella by the quadriceps tendon, and by the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
muscles.action: Knee extension; its distal oblique fibers draw the patella medially and are the principal restraint against lateral patellar tracking.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Femoral nerve (L2-L4)

muscles.name: Popliteus
muscles.origin: Lateral femoral condyle and the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of the proximal tibia, above the soleal line.
muscles.action: Unlocks the fully extended knee to begin flexion, by internally rotating the tibia on the femur with the foot free, or externally rotating the femur on the tibia with the foot planted. Assists knee flexion and draws the lateral meniscus posteriorly during flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.name: Gastrocnemius
muscles.origin: Medial head: posterior, non-articular surface of the medial femoral condyle. Lateral head: lateral surface of the lateral femoral condyle.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneal tuberosity, by the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.
muscles.action: Ankle plantarflexion, strongest with the knee extended; assists knee flexion. The explosive plantarflexor, as against the soleus's sustained postural role.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (S1-S2)

muscles.name: Soleus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the head and proximal shaft of the fibula, the soleal line, and the proximal two-thirds of the medial border of the tibia.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneal tuberosity, by the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon, joined with gastrocnemius.
muscles.action: Ankle plantarflexion, unaffected by knee position since it does not cross the knee. Predominates in sustained activity - standing, walking uphill - and is the principal postural muscle resisting forward sway.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (S1-S2)

muscles.name: Plantaris
muscles.origin: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur, just above the lateral head of gastrocnemius.
muscles.insertion: Posterior surface of the calcaneus, medial to the calcaneal tendon, or blending with it.
muscles.action: Weakly assists ankle plantarflexion and knee flexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (S1-S2)

muscles.name: Peroneus(Fibularis)Longus
muscles.origin: Superolateral surface of the fibular head, proximal two-thirds of the lateral fibular shaft, the lateral tibial condyle, and the intermuscular septum.
muscles.insertion: Base of the 1st metatarsal and the medial cuneiform, reached by crossing the sole obliquely; variant slips to the 2nd-5th metatarsals are described.
muscles.action: Foot and ankle eversion - the primary action; assists plantarflexion and maintains the lateral and transverse arches.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superficial fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5-S1)

muscles.name: Peroneus(Fibularis)Brevis
muscles.origin: Lower two-thirds of the lateral surface of the fibula and the anterior intermuscular septum.
muscles.insertion: Styloid process on the lateral aspect of the tuberosity at the base of the 5th metatarsal.
muscles.action: Foot and ankle eversion - the primary action; assists plantarflexion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superficial fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5-S2)

muscles.name: Peroneus(Fibularis)Tertius
muscles.origin: Distal anterior surface of the fibula and the adjacent interosseous membrane, often continuous with extensor digitorum longus.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the 5th metatarsal.
muscles.action: Weakly assists ankle dorsiflexion; contributes to foot eversion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5-S1)

muscles.name: ExtensorDigitorumLongus
muscles.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, the anterior surface of the fibula, and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Four tendons to the dorsal expansions of the lateral four toes, reaching the middle and distal phalanges.
muscles.action: Extension of the lateral four toes at the metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints; assists ankle dorsiflexion and foot eversion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5-S1)

muscles.name: ExtensorHallucisLongus
muscles.origin: Middle half of the anterior surface of the fibula and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Dorsal central aspect of the base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.
muscles.action: Extension of the great toe; ankle dorsiflexion; weak foot inversion.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.name: TibialisAnterior
muscles.origin: Lateral condyle of the tibia, proximal two-thirds of the lateral surface of the tibial shaft, the anterior surface of the interosseous membrane, the deep fascia cruris and the intermuscular septum.
muscles.insertion: Medial cuneiform and the base of the 1st metatarsal, on the medial border of the foot.
muscles.action: The strongest dorsiflexor of the ankle, essential during the swing phase of gait; a primary inverter of the foot, working with tibialis posterior to supinate the medial arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L4-S1)

muscles.name: TibialisPosterior
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the interosseous membrane, the proximal two-thirds of the posterior and medial surfaces of the fibula, and the superior posterior tibia.
muscles.insertion: Tuberosity of the navicular and plantar aspect of the medial cuneiform; a plantar slip to the bases of the 2nd-4th metatarsals, the intermediate and lateral cuneiforms and the cuboid; and a recurrent slip to the sustentaculum tali.
muscles.action: Foot inversion - the principal inverter - and ankle plantarflexion. Dynamically supports the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L4-L5)
muscles.review_flag: nerve root levels rest on a single source

muscles.name: FlexorDigitorumLongus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the middle third of the tibia, below the soleal line.
muscles.insertion: Plantar surfaces of the bases of the distal phalanges of the lateral four toes.
muscles.action: Flexion of the lateral four toes, the distal interphalangeal joints in particular; assists ankle plantarflexion, foot inversion and maintenance of the arches.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L5-S2)

muscles.name: Flexor Hallucis Longus
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the distal two-thirds of the fibula and the adjacent interosseous membrane.
muscles.insertion: Plantar surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the great toe.
muscles.action: Flexion of the great toe at the interphalangeal and metatarsophalangeal joints; assists ankle plantarflexion, foot inversion and arch support. Provides the final push-off in gait.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Tibial nerve (L5-S2)

muscles.name: FlexorDigitorumBrevis
muscles.origin: Calcaneal tuberosity, plantar aponeurosis and the intermuscular septa.
muscles.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of the lateral four toes, each tendon splitting to let the flexor digitorum longus tendon pass through.
muscles.action: Flexion of the lateral four toes at the proximal interphalangeal and metatarsophalangeal joints. Acts as a tie beam supporting both longitudinal arches.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial plantar nerve (S1-S2)

muscles.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi
muscles.origin: Calcaneal tuberosity, plantar aponeurosis and the intermuscular septa.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe.
muscles.action: Abduction of the little toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; acts as a tie beam maintaining the lateral longitudinal arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S1-S3)

muscles.name: FlexorHallucisBrevis
muscles.origin: Plantar surfaces of the cuboid and the lateral cuneiform, with a slip from the tendon of tibialis posterior.
muscles.insertion: Medial and lateral sides of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe, each tendon containing a sesamoid bone.
muscles.action: Flexion of the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; supports the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial plantar nerve (S1-S2)

muscles.name: AbductorHallucis
muscles.origin: Calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.
muscles.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe.
muscles.action: Abduction of the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint, with assistance in flexion; acts as a tie beam for the medial longitudinal arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Medial plantar nerve (S1-S2)

muscles.name: FlexorDigitiMinimi (Foot)
muscles.origin: Base of the 5th metatarsal and the adjacent plantar aponeurosis.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th toe.
muscles.action: Flexion of the little toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; supports the lateral longitudinal arch as a tie beam.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S2-S3)

muscles.name: QuadratusPlantae
muscles.origin: Medial and lateral plantar surfaces of the calcaneus.
muscles.insertion: Lateral border of the tendon of flexor digitorum longus.
muscles.action: Redirects the oblique pull of flexor digitorum longus into the sagittal plane, so the toes flex straight rather than deviating medially; assists flexion of the distal phalanges of the lateral four toes.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S1-S3)

muscles.name: Lumbricals (Foot)
muscles.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum longus.
muscles.insertion: Medial extensor expansions on the proximal phalanges of the lateral four toes.
muscles.action: Flexion at the metatarsophalangeal joints with extension at the interphalangeal joints; prevent buckling of the toes and give dynamic support to all the arches.
muscles.nerve_innervation: 1st lumbrical: medial plantar nerve (S1-S2). 2nd, 3rd and 4th: lateral plantar nerve (S2-S3)

muscles.name: AdductorHallucis
muscles.origin: Oblique head: bases of the 2nd-4th metatarsals. Transverse head: metatarsophalangeal ligaments of the 3rd-5th toes.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe.
muscles.action: Adduction of the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint; acts as an intersegmental tie and a tie beam for the anterior transverse arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep branch of the lateral plantar nerve (S2-S3)

muscles.name: PlantarInterossei
muscles.origin: Medial sides of the shafts and bases of the 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsals.
muscles.insertion: Medial sides of the bases of the proximal phalanges of the 3rd, 4th and 5th toes.
muscles.action: Adduction of the 3rd, 4th and 5th toes toward the axis of the foot, taken through the 2nd toe; flexion at the metatarsophalangeal joints, and assistance to the lumbricals in extending the interphalangeal joints.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S2-S3)

muscles.name: Dorsal Interossei (Foot)
muscles.origin: Each by two heads from the adjacent sides of the shafts of two metatarsals.
muscles.insertion: Bases of the proximal phalanges and the extensor expansions of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th toes - the 1st to the medial side of the 2nd toe, the others to the lateral sides.
muscles.action: Abduction of the 2nd, 3rd and 4th toes away from the axis of the foot, taken through the 2nd toe; assist flexion at the metatarsophalangeal joints and dorsiflexion by the extensor tendons. Act as intersegmental ties for the anterior transverse arch.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Lateral plantar nerve (S2-S3)

muscles.name: ExtensorDigitorumBrevis
muscles.origin: Dorsolateral surface of the calcaneus, the inferior extensor retinaculum and the talocalcaneal interosseous ligament.
muscles.insertion: Extensor expansions of the 2nd-4th toes; the most medial slip, named extensor hallucis brevis, reaches the base of the proximal phalanx of the great toe.
muscles.action: Extension of the 2nd-4th toes; the medial slip extends the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve (L5-S1)

muscles.name: Piriformis
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the sacrum, the gluteal surface of the ilium near the margin of the greater sciatic notch, the capsule of the sacroiliac joint, and sometimes the sacrotuberous ligament.
muscles.insertion: Superior aspect of the greater trochanter of the femur, with the tendons of obturator internus and the gemelli.
muscles.action: External rotation of the thigh with the hip extended; abduction of the flexed hip, which in walking shifts body weight and prevents falling. Stabilizes the femoral head in the acetabulum.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior rami of S1-S2 (nerve to piriformis); variants from S2 alone or L5-S2

muscles.name: Gemellus Superior
muscles.origin: Ischial spine.
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter of the femur, in conjunction with obturator internus.
muscles.action: External rotation of the hip; abduction of the flexed hip; stabilizes the femoral head in the acetabulum.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to obturator internus (L4-S2)

muscles.name: Obturator Internus
muscles.origin: Pelvic surface of the obturator membrane and the rami surrounding the obturator foramen.
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter of the femur, by a conjoint tendon with the gemelli.
muscles.action: External rotation of the hip, particularly when extended; abduction of the flexed hip; stabilizes the femoral head in the acetabulum.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to obturator internus (L5-S2)

muscles.name: Gemellus Inferior
muscles.origin: Ischial tuberosity, at its upper part.
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the greater trochanter of the femur, by the conjoint tendon shared with obturator internus and gemellus superior.
muscles.action: External rotation of the hip; abduction of the flexed hip; stabilizes the femoral head in the acetabulum.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to quadratus femoris (L4-S1)

muscles.name: Obturator Externus
muscles.origin: Bony margin of the obturator foramen on the external surface of the pelvis, with fibers from the obturator membrane.
muscles.insertion: Trochanteric fossa on the medial surface of the greater trochanter, by a cylindrical tendon.
muscles.action: External rotation of the hip in neutral or flexed positions; assists adduction of the flexed hip; stabilizes the femoral head.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Obturator nerve, posterior branch (L2-L4)

muscles.name: Quadratus Femoris
muscles.origin: Upper part of the lateral border of the ischial tuberosity.
muscles.insertion: Quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest of the femur, above the adductor magnus attachment.
muscles.action: External rotation of the thigh at the hip; stabilizes the femoral head in the acetabulum; assists adduction.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to quadratus femoris (L4-S1)

muscles.name: Frontalis
muscles.origin: Epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica); it has no bony attachment.
muscles.insertion: Skin and superficial fascia of the eyebrow and lower forehead, interlacing with procerus, corrugator supercilii and orbicularis oculi.
muscles.action: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead transversely; acting with occipitalis it moves the scalp.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Temporal (frontal) branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: Occipitalis
muscles.origin: Lateral two-thirds of the superior nuchal line of the occipital bone.
muscles.insertion: Epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica).
muscles.action: Draws the scalp backward; working with frontalis it helps raise the eyebrows and wrinkle the forehead.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Posterior auricular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: OrbicularisOculi
muscles.origin: Orbital part: nasal part of the frontal bone, frontal process of the maxilla and the medial palpebral ligament. Palpebral part: medial palpebral ligament. Lacrimal (deep) part: posterior lacrimal crest, behind the lacrimal sac.
muscles.insertion: Orbital part: encircles the orbit and blends with the skin and soft tissue around it. Palpebral part: lateral palpebral raphe. Lacrimal part: the tarsal plates and lateral palpebral raphe.
muscles.action: Closes the eyelids: the palpebral part gently (blinking, sleep), the orbital part forcefully (squeezing the eyes shut). The lacrimal part draws the lids medially and helps pump tears into the lacrimal sac.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Temporal and zygomatic branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: CorrugatorSupercilii
muscles.origin: Medial end of the superciliary arch of the frontal bone.
muscles.insertion: Skin of the middle and medial part of the eyebrow.
muscles.action: Draws the eyebrows medially and downward, producing vertical frown lines between them.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Temporal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII); contributions from the zygomatic and buccal branches are described

muscles.name: Procerus
muscles.origin: Fascia over the lower nasal bone and the upper part of the lateral nasal cartilage.
muscles.insertion: Skin between the eyebrows (glabella), blending with frontalis.
muscles.action: Pulls the medial ends of the eyebrows downward, producing horizontal wrinkles across the root of the nose.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII), temporal branch; buccal and zygomatic contributions are also described

muscles.name: Nasalis
muscles.origin: Maxilla above the incisor and canine teeth, beside the nasal notch.
muscles.insertion: Transverse part: the nasal aponeurosis across the bridge of the nose. Alar part: the ala of the nose.
muscles.action: Transverse part compresses the nasal aperture; alar part draws the ala outward and flares the nostril.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)
muscles.review_flag: attachments rest on a single source

muscles.name: DepressorSeptiNasi
muscles.origin: Incisive fossa of the maxilla, just above the central incisor teeth.
muscles.insertion: Mobile part of the nasal septum.
muscles.action: Draws the nasal septum and tip downward, helping to widen the nostrils.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: OrbicularisOris
muscles.origin: No bony or tendinous origin: fibers arise from the modiolus at each corner of the mouth and from the skin, fascia and muscles converging on the lips.
muscles.insertion: Skin and mucous membrane of the lips; upper (nasal) bundles also attach near the anterior nasal spine and the nasal septum.
muscles.action: Closes and purses the lips and presses them against the teeth; shapes the lips for speech, sucking, whistling and keeping food in the mouth.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal and marginal mandibular branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: LevatorLabiiSuperioris
muscles.origin: Infraorbital margin of the maxilla, above the infraorbital foramen, extending onto the zygomatic bone.
muscles.insertion: Skin and muscle of the upper lip.
muscles.action: Elevates and everts the upper lip and deepens the nasolabial fold.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: LevatorLabiiSuperiorisAlaequeNasi
muscles.origin: Upper part of the frontal process of the maxilla.
muscles.insertion: Two slips: one to the skin and cartilage of the nasal ala, one to the skin and muscle of the upper lip.
muscles.action: Elevates and everts the upper lip and dilates the nostril.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: ZygomaticusMajor
muscles.origin: Lateral surface of the zygomatic bone, in front of the zygomaticotemporal suture.
muscles.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth, interlacing with the other muscles there.
muscles.action: Draws the angle of the mouth upward and laterally, as in smiling.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: ZygomaticusMinor
muscles.origin: Lateral surface of the zygomatic bone, just behind the zygomaticomaxillary suture and medial to zygomaticus major.
muscles.insertion: Skin and muscle of the lateral upper lip, medial to the insertion of zygomaticus major.
muscles.action: Elevates the upper lip, showing the upper teeth, and deepens the nasolabial fold.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: LevatorAnguliOris
muscles.origin: Canine fossa of the maxilla, below the infraorbital foramen.
muscles.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
muscles.action: Raises the angle of the mouth, helping to show the upper teeth in smiling.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII), entering on its superficial surface

muscles.name: Risorius
muscles.origin: Fascia of the lateral cheek over the parotid gland and masseter, variably from the platysma fascia.
muscles.insertion: Skin at the angle of the mouth (modiolus).
muscles.action: Draws the angle of the mouth laterally.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal branch of the facial nerve (CN VII); a marginal mandibular contribution is described

muscles.name: Buccinator
muscles.origin: Alveolar processes of the maxilla and mandible opposite the molar teeth, and the pterygomandibular raphe.
muscles.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth, blending with orbicularis oris into both lips.
muscles.action: Presses the cheek against the teeth, keeping food between the molars; draws the angle of the mouth laterally; used in blowing and sucking.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: DepressorAnguliOris
muscles.origin: Oblique line of the mandible and the mental tubercle.
muscles.insertion: Modiolus at the angle of the mouth.
muscles.action: Draws the angle of the mouth downward and laterally.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Marginal mandibular and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: DepressorLabiiInferioris
muscles.origin: Oblique line of the mandible, between the symphysis and the mental foramen.
muscles.insertion: Skin and mucosa of the lower lip, blending with its partner and orbicularis oris.
muscles.action: Draws the lower lip downward and laterally and everts it.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: Mentalis
muscles.origin: Incisive fossa of the mandible, below the lower incisor teeth.
muscles.insertion: Skin of the chin.
muscles.action: Raises and wrinkles the skin of the chin, elevating and protruding the lower lip.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: Platysma
muscles.origin: Superficial fascia over the upper pectoralis major and deltoid (upper chest and shoulder).
muscles.insertion: Inferior border of the mandible, the skin of the lower face and the angle of the mouth, blending with depressor anguli oris and orbicularis oris.
muscles.action: Tenses the skin of the neck; draws the corners of the mouth and the lower lip downward; assists depression of the mandible.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Cervical branch of the facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: Masseter
muscles.origin: Zygomatic arch - chiefly the lower border of its anterior two-thirds - and the zygomatic bone.
muscles.insertion: Lateral surface of the ramus and angle of the mandible, extending up toward the coronoid process.
muscles.action: Elevates the mandible to close the jaw and clench the teeth; superficial fibers assist protrusion, deeper fibers assist retraction.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Masseteric nerve, from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3)

muscles.name: Temporalis
muscles.origin: Floor of the temporal fossa up to the inferior temporal line, and the deep surface of the temporal fascia.
muscles.insertion: Coronoid process and anterior border of the ramus of the mandible, by a tendon passing deep to the zygomatic arch.
muscles.action: Elevates the mandible; its posterior fibers retract it.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Deep temporal nerves, from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3)

muscles.name: MedialPterygoid
muscles.origin: Deep head: medial surface of the lateral pterygoid plate of the sphenoid and the pyramidal process of the palatine bone. Superficial head: tuberosity of the maxilla.
muscles.insertion: Medial surface of the ramus and angle of the mandible.
muscles.action: Elevates and protrudes the mandible; with the lateral pterygoid, moves the jaw from side to side in grinding.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to medial pterygoid, from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3)

muscles.name: LateralPterygoid
muscles.origin: Superior head: infratemporal surface of the greater wing of the sphenoid. Inferior head: lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate.
muscles.insertion: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the mandibular condyle; the superior head also reaches the articular disc and capsule of the temporomandibular joint.
muscles.action: Protrudes the mandible and draws the condyle forward as the mouth opens; produces side-to-side grinding movements.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to lateral pterygoid, from the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve (CN V3)

muscles.name: LevatorPalpebraeSuperioris
muscles.origin: Lesser wing of the sphenoid, above and in front of the optic canal.
muscles.insertion: Through its aponeurosis into the skin of the upper eyelid and the anterior surface of the superior tarsal plate; a smooth-muscle slip (superior tarsal muscle) attaches to the upper margin of the tarsal plate.
muscles.action: Raises and holds up the upper eyelid.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III); the superior tarsal smooth-muscle slip is supplied by sympathetic fibers

muscles.name: SuperiorRectus
muscles.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) at the apex of the orbit.
muscles.insertion: Sclera on the upper surface of the eyeball, about 7.7 mm behind the limbus.
muscles.action: Elevates the eye (chiefly when it is abducted); also adducts and intorts it.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Superior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)

muscles.name: InferiorRectus
muscles.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) at the apex of the orbit.
muscles.insertion: Sclera on the lower surface of the eyeball, about 6.5 mm behind the limbus.
muscles.action: Depresses the eye; also extorts and adducts it.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)

muscles.name: MedialRectus
muscles.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) at the apex of the orbit.
muscles.insertion: Sclera on the medial surface of the eyeball, about 5.5 mm behind the limbus.
muscles.action: Adducts the eye.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)

muscles.name: LateralRectus
muscles.origin: Common tendinous ring (annulus of Zinn) at the apex of the orbit.
muscles.insertion: Sclera on the lateral surface of the eyeball, about 6.9 mm behind the limbus.
muscles.action: Abducts the eye.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Abducens nerve (CN VI)

muscles.name: SuperiorOblique
muscles.origin: Body of the sphenoid, superomedial to the optic canal and above the common tendinous ring.
muscles.insertion: Its tendon passes through the trochlea at the superomedial orbital margin, turns backward and laterally, and inserts on the sclera of the posterior superolateral quadrant of the eyeball, beneath the superior rectus.
muscles.action: Intorts, depresses and abducts the eye; its depressing action is greatest when the eye is adducted.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Trochlear nerve (CN IV)

muscles.name: InferiorOblique
muscles.origin: Orbital surface of the maxilla in the floor of the orbit, near the orbital rim and lateral to the nasolacrimal groove.
muscles.insertion: Sclera of the posterior inferolateral quadrant of the eyeball, near the macula.
muscles.action: Extorts, elevates and abducts the eye.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (CN III)

muscles.name: Genioglossus
muscles.origin: Superior mental spine (genial tubercle) on the inner surface of the mandibular symphysis.
muscles.insertion: Fans into the tongue from tip to root along its dorsum, through the lingual aponeurosis; the lowest fibers reach the body of the hyoid bone.
muscles.action: Protrudes the tongue and depresses its central part; acting on one side, deviates the tongue to the opposite side.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

muscles.name: Hyoglossus
muscles.origin: Body and greater horn of the hyoid bone.
muscles.insertion: Side of the posterior half of the tongue, between styloglossus laterally and the inferior longitudinal muscle medially.
muscles.action: Depresses and retracts the tongue.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

muscles.name: Styloglossus
muscles.origin: Anterior surface of the styloid process near its tip, and the stylomandibular ligament.
muscles.insertion: Lateral side of the tongue along its length.
muscles.action: Retracts the tongue and elevates its sides.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

muscles.name: Palatoglossus
muscles.origin: Oral (inferior) surface of the palatine aponeurosis of the soft palate.
muscles.insertion: Posterolateral part of the tongue, some fibers blending with the transverse intrinsic muscle.
muscles.action: Elevates the back of the tongue and draws the soft palate down, narrowing the oropharyngeal isthmus.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Pharyngeal branch of the vagus nerve (CN X), via the pharyngeal plexus

muscles.name: IntrinsicTongueMuscles
muscles.origin: Entirely within the tongue, with no bony attachment: superior and inferior longitudinal bundles beneath the dorsal and ventral surfaces, transverse fibers from the median septum, vertical fibers from the dorsal submucosa.
muscles.insertion: Within the tongue: longitudinal fibers toward the tip, transverse fibers to the lateral margins, vertical fibers to the underside.
muscles.action: Change the shape of the tongue: the longitudinal muscles shorten it and curl the tip up (superior) or down (inferior); the transverse muscle narrows and lengthens it; the vertical muscle flattens and broadens it.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

muscles.name: Digastric
muscles.origin: Anterior belly: digastric fossa on the inner lower border of the mandible near the symphysis. Posterior belly: mastoid notch of the temporal bone.
muscles.insertion: Intermediate tendon, held to the hyoid bone at the junction of its body and greater horn by a fibrous sling.
muscles.action: Depresses the mandible to open the mouth when the hyoid is fixed; elevates the hyoid during swallowing.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Anterior belly: nerve to mylohyoid, from the inferior alveolar nerve (CN V3). Posterior belly: facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: Mylohyoid
muscles.origin: Mylohyoid line of the mandible, from the symphysis back to the last molar.
muscles.insertion: Median fibrous raphe running from the symphysis to the hyoid, and the body of the hyoid bone.
muscles.action: Raises the floor of the mouth, the tongue and the hyoid in swallowing and speech; depresses the mandible when the hyoid is fixed.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Nerve to mylohyoid, a branch of the inferior alveolar nerve (CN V3)

muscles.name: Stylohyoid
muscles.origin: Styloid process of the temporal bone.
muscles.insertion: Body of the hyoid at its junction with the greater horn, splitting around the intermediate tendon of the digastric.
muscles.action: Elevates and retracts the hyoid, lengthening the floor of the mouth during swallowing.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Facial nerve (CN VII)

muscles.name: Geniohyoid
muscles.origin: Inferior mental spine (genial tubercle) of the mandible.
muscles.insertion: Anterior surface of the body of the hyoid bone.
muscles.action: Draws the hyoid upward and forward, widening the pharynx; depresses the mandible when the hyoid is fixed.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Fibers of the C1 ventral ramus carried by the hypoglossal nerve

muscles.name: Sternohyoid
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the manubrium and the sternal end of the clavicle.
muscles.insertion: Lower border of the body of the hyoid, medial to the omohyoid.
muscles.action: Depresses the hyoid after swallowing and in speech.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Ansa cervicalis (C1-C3)

muscles.name: Omohyoid
muscles.origin: Inferior belly: upper border of the scapula, near the suprascapular notch.
muscles.insertion: Superior belly: lower border of the body of the hyoid, lateral to the sternohyoid. The two bellies are joined by an intermediate tendon.
muscles.action: Depresses and steadies the hyoid bone.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Ansa cervicalis (C1-C3)

muscles.name: Sternothyroid
muscles.origin: Posterior surface of the manubrium, below the origin of the sternohyoid.
muscles.insertion: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
muscles.action: Depresses the larynx (thyroid cartilage).
muscles.nerve_innervation: Ansa cervicalis (C1-C3)

muscles.name: Thyrohyoid
muscles.origin: Oblique line of the thyroid cartilage.
muscles.insertion: Lower border of the body and the greater horn of the hyoid bone.
muscles.action: Depresses the hyoid; when the hyoid is fixed, raises the larynx.
muscles.nerve_innervation: Fibers of the C1 ventral ramus carried by the hypoglossal nerve, leaving it distal to the superior root of the ansa cervicalis
